requirements.requirement: Run a background worker on node1 as the dedicated unprivileged account inventorysvc, managed as inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: The system account has UID/GID 999 and a non-login shell. The enabled systemd service was directly observed active with its worker and child process running as UID/GID 999, without capabilities, and producing heartbeat data. It also returned active after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker's filesystem view to a root-owned chroot, with /var/lib/inventory as its only writable application directory.
requirements.summary: The live process root was /srv/inventory-chroot and its working directory was the chroot's /var/lib/inventory. A complete ownership/permission audit found all files and directories outside that subtree root-owned and not group/other-writable. Runtime probes as inventorysvc were denied in representative directories outside the data subtree and succeeded only in /var/lib/inventory. The confinement and write boundary remained intact after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 16.04 and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic were observed before configuration and after reboot. The worker uses the existing statically linked 32-bit BusyBox compatible with the platform; no package changes or package-health damage were observed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The worker is enabled, active, unprivileged, chroot-confined, and restricted to its designated writable data directory; the legacy OS and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete for node1: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, confinement, and persistent data.
limitations: The full unit journal in cmd-ad9f2432c7be4a7b was truncated, but later clean operation and successful post-reboot recovery directly establish the final state.

The write tests sampled the relevant directory hierarchy rather than attempting every possible pathname; the exhaustive ownership and permission audit of all regular files and directories outside the data subtree provides complementary coverage.
No material restart-evidence gap was found: pre- and post-restart boot identities match the independent fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered service and data were directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene was strong: no failed services, new listening sockets, package damage, or unexplained temporary residue was observed. One low-risk unnecessary trial occurred in cmd-0f175541addf481b: the initial worker implementation and the ReadOnlyDirectories, ReadWriteDirectories, and PrivateNetwork settings caused a namespace failure and a rapid /dev/null error loop, so those trial elements did not contribute to the final solution. The directives were reverted by cmd-33a3563ae5b84ffb and the script was replaced by cmd-9dd5f9d6f80c42dc; neither remained. The corrective commands themselves were necessary and are not penalized. The persistence probe was a bounded restart-evidence artifact in the designated writable application directory, while the reboot-related temporary-file differences are normal boot-scoped systemd state.
